title: SGD on a narrow loss bowl: keep paths and compare runs
description: A long, narrow bowl-shaped loss surface, long from left to right and steep from front to back. A red ball takes stochastic gradient descent steps on it and leaves an orange path behind it. A purple arrow on the ball shows the next step, which is minus the learning rate times the noisy slope. Up to three kept paths stay on the surface as faded copies in grey, green and magenta, so you can compare runs. A dark dot marks the lowest point. Readouts show the loss, the run status, the step count and the size of the noisy slope.

actions.label: Keep path and start new run

assumptions: This is an illustration: a made-up bowl formula and simulated noise, not a real model trained on data.

Loss = 0.5 × (x² + 5y²). x runs left to right, y (the steep direction) runs front to back. The surface is drawn at 0.35 × loss over x from −3 to 3 and y from −1.5 to 1.5. Plain descent is stable only for learning rates below 2/5 = 0.4.

Each step: slope estimate = true slope + noise × a random normal value per direction; step = −rate × estimate. The values come from the fixed seed in order across runs, so after a Reset they repeat. With noise, a step can go uphill.
A run ends at 200 steps (finished), when loss < 0.001 (converged), or when the ball leaves the drawn surface (diverged). Off-surface path points are drawn at the rim.
Changed from plan: the path marks every step (up to 201 points) instead of one every 4 steps (50 markers), so the zig-zag isn't hidden; each kept path also keeps every step.

The purple arrow is the next step (−rate × noisy slope), drawn 3 times its true length. It is hidden when the run has ended, and near the minimum a tiny step can be too short to draw; the slope readout still shows its size.
Changing the starting point moves the ball right away only before the first step. Otherwise it applies to the next run you start with Keep path.
Kept paths: grey is the oldest, green the middle, magenta the latest. Only the three latest are shown.
